packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, isolated image-only reader (Claude Code subagent)
text:
PACKET-09 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of
this text. I opened only PROMPT.md and the eight image files of this packet (I
did run one directory listing of the four packet directories to learn the image
filenames; packet.json was not opened).

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)

Observations
- image-001 is the overview: the spine/joint area of a small bound volume
  (ruler shows c. 13 cm height) with a colour target. Near the head of the
  spine a small rectangular piece of written material (roughly 2 cm wide by
  3 cm high by the ruler) is pasted over the joint, held under two alum-tawed /
  parchment thongs. It is a binding reinforcement, not a leaf.
- image-002, -004, -006 are closer views of that same piece from three angles
  (002 flat-on; 004 and 006 with the cover lifted, raking light). They show the
  SAME lines; they are not additional text.
- The piece carries 8 line-remnants of a rather large, upright, formal gothic
  bookhand (textualis type), brown ink, well spaced. Both the left and right
  edges of the strip cut through the lines, so every line is a mid-line
  fragment of perhaps 8-12 letters. The top line is sliced through its upper
  half by the thong.
- One letter in line 4 is touched with red, and there is a second faint red
  stroke further right in the same line. A mid-line point (punctus) follows the
  red-touched letter. No rubric, no enlarged initial, no running title, no
  underlining, no gloss visible.
- image-004 and -006 show that the piece continues to the left, round the
  joint into the spine, as a darker, abraded panel with further line-remnants
  aligned with the same 8 lines (so the visible panel is the right part of a
  wider strip). That left panel is very rubbed and crossed by sewing thread.
- image-003, -005, -007, -008 show a SECOND, separate strip lower down inside
  the lifted cover, curled, with a smaller and more compressed gothic script
  (different module, lighter brown ink). Only 3-5 line-ends/beginnings are
  exposed, obliquely and partly out of focus. image-007 also shows a third
  dark panel deep in the joint with a few lines of small script, out of focus.

Tentative interpretation (not observation)
- Larger script: possibly a liturgical or biblical book in a formal hand, given
  the size of the letters and the red stroking; this is a guess from script
  size alone. Number of columns cannot be determined from a strip this narrow.
- Smaller script on the lower strip: could be from a different manuscript, or
  a different text block of the same binder's waste; cannot be decided.

2. AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
Selected: all 8 lines of the upper pasted piece (image-002, checked against
image-004 and image-006); the exposed line-ends on the lower curled strip
(image-005, image-003, image-007).
Unread: the left (spine-side) continuation of the upper piece, visible in
image-004/-006, where I can see ink but cannot resolve letters with any
confidence; the dark panel deep in the joint in image-007.

3. TRANSCRIPTION

A. Upper pasted piece. Line numbers count from the top of image-002. The same
lines recur in image-004 and image-006 (overlap, not new text). Both ends of
every line are cut. Minims are heavily blurred; almost every reading below is
uncertain and is given as letter-shapes rather than as words.

image-002 L1: [upper half cut] ...ȝ(?) . m(?)[...
image-002 L2: ...]im(?)us(?) ⁊(?) agen(?)[...     (alt.: ...]mia(?) Sager(?)[ )
image-002 L3: ...]i(?) iudo(?)ꝝ(?) ui(?) ca(?)r(?)[...   (a superscript mark or
              ascender stands above the 3rd-4th letter; alt. "...mid(?)o...")
image-002 L4: ...]mi(?)nis(?) G/S(?, red-touched) · t(?)er(?)ri(?) a(?)[...
              (a second red stroke before the last visible letter)
image-002 L5: ...]b(?)e(?)r(?) : i(?)m(?) to(?) . o(?)[...   (tall letter with
              cross-stroke, t or ſt, in the middle of the line)
image-002 L6: ...]ʒ(?)iuml(?)au(?) teʒ(?) leg(?)[...   (alt. first group:
              "ſumi-", "ꝯiun-"; an ascender l or h after the minims)
image-002 L7: ...]ua(?) vn(?)ʒ(?)iamus(?) [...   (alt. "vrgiamus", "-giauius";
              descender on the 3rd letter of the second word)
image-002 L8: ...]ſ(?)to ꝯ(?)[2-3 letters]p(?)minus(?)[...   (alt. ending
              "-manus", "-mouis")

Checks against the other angles:
image-004 L2-L8 = image-002 L2-L8. In image-004 L6 the opening group looks like
"ſum(m)lau" / "ʒiumlau" again; L7 "[.]ua vngia(?)uus"; L8 "[.]ſto ..." - no
improvement. image-006 (raking) L4 shows the red-touched letter as a round
closed form (G, S or a 2-shaped letter) preceded by "...mi/ni" - no improvement.

Left continuation of the same lines (image-004, image-006, left of the fold):
ink traces on all 8 lines; isolated shapes only, e.g. a possible "d"/"a" on the
level of L5 and "..ua" joining L7. [illegible] - this is a limit of the
abraded, thread-covered surface in these photographs.

B. Lower curled strip (smaller script). Lines counted from the first exposed
line on the strip, not from the image top, because the strip sits low in an
oblique frame.

image-005, strip L1: ...]ip̄(?) mut(?) a(?)[...     (= image-003 "ip̄mut a")
image-005, strip L2: ...]ꝑ(?) pmur(?)[...            (= image-003 "pmre"?)
image-005, strip L3: ...]lis(?) : ng(?)[...
image-005, strip L4: ...]nuly(?)[...
image-007 (same strip from the other side, out of focus):
image-007, strip L1: ...]p̄(?) bat(?)[...
image-007, strip L2: ...]⁊(?) ꝑ . ro(?) . q(?)[...
image-007, strip L3: ...]da(?)[...
image-008 is a tighter crop of the image-007 area and adds nothing legible.

4. LIMITATIONS
- No complete word is read with confidence in either piece. I could not
  determine the language securely from the upper piece (Latin is the default
  assumption for the script type; the shapes in L6-L7 did not resolve into
  confident Latin words and I have not forced them).
- Every line is cut at both ends; the top line is half-covered; ink has bled
  into the fibrous surface so minims merge.
- The lower strip is seen only obliquely and partly out of focus.
- Useful additional imaging: a flat, in-focus, higher-magnification shot of the
  upper piece with the thong lifted (for L1), a transmitted-light or infrared
  image to separate the minims, and a flat view of the lower curled strip
  uncurled, plus the spine-side continuation of the upper piece.
- This is an unverified image reading. I did nothing beyond the stated rules
  other than the directory listing noted above.
